correctness.rationale: The defining weighted BMO quotient is controlled by two exhaustive box regimes. Small/far boxes give the exact local scale L^(1-s), while comparable/large boxes give the global decay scale L^(-r-s). Two separate rescaled box families produce positive matching lower asymptotics, proving necessity and endpoint non-vanishing. The source analytic-symbol theorems then convert the exact BMOA and VMOA classification into boundedness and compactness of both Bergman commutators.

value.rationale: Power weights and Cauchy-pole symbols are canonical scale models for the source's two-weight theory. The exact classification separates a local regularity obstruction from a global decay obstruction and identifies a sharp bounded-but-noncompact boundary on both sides. This is a natural complete model calculation that makes the abstract theorem quantitatively transparent and constrains any broader two-weight classification.
